feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the technical/strategic blend is compelling. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on outcome-based achievements beyond a few metrics, and could be streamlined for sharper impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility and leadership credibility.  
- Strong mix of strategy, operations, content, web platforms, analytics, and multimedia, which supports the “lead” positioning well.  
- Generally clean, professional writing with good specificity on platforms and scale (e.g., 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, analytics stack).

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include impact such as growth, efficiency gains, engagement improvements, cost savings, or adoption metrics.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency fixes: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement”); standardize punctuation in lists; “French (A2/learning)” would be stylistically cleaner than “A2/Learning.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and anchoring it more explicitly to public-sector/advocacy work would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with sharper, evidence-aligned positioning tied to digital transformation, governance, and mission-driven communications.
- Add public-sector or membership-organization context to better reflect the NACo experience.
- Keep it to 2 sentences for a stronger opening.

Suggested rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and public-sector-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, CMS and platform modernization, editorial workflow design, and stakeholder coordination, with a strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear, accessible advocacy content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” is broad; consider using “public-sector and advocacy organizations” for specificity.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “CMS strategy, governance & administration.”
- Group related items to reduce repetition and improve flow: strategy/governance, platforms/workflows, analytics, stakeholder communication, multimedia.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout for consistency.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS strategy, governance & administration • Editorial workflows & content operations • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Workflow architecture & systems improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy, policy & member communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items duplicate Topline Skills; consider shortening or removing this section if space is tight.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting-level outcomes, systems leadership, and 2–3 signature initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, Drupal platform improvements, and AI-enabled member discovery.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed/implemented/refined” instead of “consult/build/develop/deliver/advise.”
- Consolidate into 4 bullets max, e.g.:
- Designed digital governance, workflows, and analytics systems to improve cross-channel communications operations.
- Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and technical troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages supported, launch dates, traffic, adoption, time saved, or engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level if those projects remain.
- Governance/analytics/platform improvement also overlaps with Director of Digital Media; emphasize advisory/consulting scope here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational scope, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Make the website bullet the anchor achievement: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add outcomes where possible for analytics/governance/video: e.g., faster reporting, reduced reliance on vendors, improved publishing consistency, increased production volume, or stronger campaign performance.
- Tighten channel language: replace “reaching tens of thousands…” with a more outcome-driven line tied to engagement, advocacy reach, or audience growth if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building the in-house studio/capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scope so it shows clear growth into the Director role.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper systems line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows by coordinating communications, advocacy and program teams around more consistent digital production processes.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” partially duplicates the earlier “Digital Media Manager / Producer” entry; frame this here as scaling/operationalizing the series.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, differentiated language tied to leadership scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector advocacy messaging & audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations” or “Publishing workflows,” which better reflects the CV’s strongest recent experience.
- Keep wording parallel and specific; avoid standalone soft phrases like “focused” unless paired with an operational outcome.
- If space allows, use “enterprise web modernization” instead of “enterprise digital strategy” to align with the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems and governance” duplicates Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles; keep only if this section needs sector positioning.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages
- Enterprise CMS modernization & front-end implementation
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript/jQuery
- API integrations, workflow automation & Airtable-based systems
- AI-enabled search and content discovery
- Put Drupal first and keep AI-enabled search near the end for emphasis on recent, high-impact work.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, swap one generic item for a stronger outcome-oriented phrase like “large-scale Drupal migrations” or “modular microsite builds.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save detailed tools there.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact wording.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity for analytics infrastructure, dashboarding and user-behavior analysis”
- Replace generic items with stronger phrasing: “KPI framework development” instead of “KPI design”; “executive reporting” instead of “leadership reporting”

- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrase.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and recent in-house studio/event delivery impact rather than listing basic production tasks.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light proficiency/context instead of just naming tools, e.g. **Drupal (migration, microsites, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, split by strength: **Primary: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint | Working: Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep “Drupal” first; it is the clearest platform anchor across recent roles and projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry; consider removing one or making this version more technical/proficiency-based.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical range, but this reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent work and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations & tagging: API integrations, Google Tag Manager • Edge/serverless & deployment: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers unless they matter; “HTML” and “CSS” are usually cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets rather than here, e.g., “built custom Drupal microsites,” “automated deployments,” or “implemented tagging across high-traffic sites.”
- Consider replacing jQuery with a more current framing if usage is limited: “JavaScript (including legacy jQuery environments).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM overlaps conceptually with analytics infrastructure elsewhere; keep it here only if you’ve implemented tagging directly.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than reinforcing your stronger positioning in workflow automation and cross-team operations. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**.
- Reorder by relevance to your recent work and group by function: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just listing tools: **Workflow automation, intake tracking, editorial planning and cross-team collaboration using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Slack and Teams**
- Consider dropping one lower-value/older tool (e.g. Basecamp) unless you used it recently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless tied to operational systems or collaboration workflows.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of current email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize enterprise-grade systems over basic tools.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by relevance/scale: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp”
- If accurate, sharpen the label to: “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms”
- Consider adding functional context instead of just names: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign delivery, newsletter operations, audience engagement)”
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, put it first and consider dropping the least relevant/oldest tool to keep the section tighter.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding newsletter scale or channel-management claims here; those are already covered well in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 experience entries.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” production volume, or workflow improvements achieved at this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Split the second sentence into clearer impact points: website refresh, recurring video/livestream production, and team/process support.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social support volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if retained here, frame this as launching or piloting the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo entries; specify what changed or drop it here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy-support projects for NACo programs while expanding the organization’s early digital content capabilities.”
- Replace vague phrasing with action + scope: “Produced multimedia and digital content for program and policy initiatives, supporting organizational communications and member engagement.”
- Make the podcast launch the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one metric or output count: number of episodes, audience/downloads, projects supported, or teams/programs served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item lighter and more foundational.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social leadership here, since those are covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
